newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich nudges higher after results.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich nudges higher after results.

text.p: Shares in building society-turned bank Woolwich Plc made modest gains on Wednesday after posting first half profits that were slightly above analysts expectations.
The shares rose 2-1/2p to 294-1/2p by 0745 GMT.
"The figures were no disaster but were flattered by not allowing as much for bad debt as they might have done," said one dealer.
"There was nothing particularly sparkling about the results and the shares probably don't have far to go in the short term because there's still a lot of stock to be absorbed," he added.

In its first set of results since becoming a publicly listed company, Woolwich said first-half pre-tax profits had risen to 187.8 million stg from 183.1 million a year ago. A dividend of 3p per share was slightly above expectations and provision for bad debt fell from 22.9 to 7.2 million stg.
Analysts had forecast profits of 180-185 million stg.
